reference.oracle: Same existing D3D9 implementation compiled into a private static archive,consumed by a real loader DLL. Build artifact assertions verify namespace,stdcall ABI,no CRT/system D3D9 dependency and separate trace path. Relational reference requires global uniqueness for all six device/declaration handles,the same session tuple across three module Hellos,and a single final SessionEnd after explicit destruction. SDK factory QI/GetDirect3D identities and exact final refs prove real COM objects. Expected pixels are independent constant colors,not derived from captured data.
reference.scope: Stage4K1 prepares a linkable D3D9 core with prefixed factory/module lifecycle API and retail/diagnostic21-member archives including shared runtime. Minimal consumer exposes exactly one factory export. Ordinary DLL public exports remain intact,private diagnostics use distinct d3d9_core_trace filenames,and D3D8 headers can include forward-declared boundary without mixing SDK types. XP loads/unloads private consumer twice while ordinary D3D9 device stays alive,using three factories/devices,three cache declarations,three Hellos in one owner/session and five UP/readbacks;only one final session/owner end. Dual GPU validates320 pixels and empty maps before SessionEnd and genuine owner release. Actual D3D8 device/resource wrapping,PP/caps/state conversions,full identity mapping,HAL/games/FPS and stages4/5/6 remain open. D3D8/DDraw and host/protocol/shader/bundle unchanged.

xp.rendering: Same D3D9 implementation linked into a minimal private consumer DLL and coexisting with ordinary D3D9.DLL. Private DLL loads twice/unloads twice while ordinary device stays live and draws after each detach; three factories/devices preserve COM parent identity and final refs. validationRepairs: Private mode compiles the same D3D9 implementation with prefixed factory/loader symbols; ordinary compatibility exports are excluded only in that mode. Shared runtime members are packaged once in a fresh archive. D3D8 SDK header compiles with the boundary; actual SDK types stay in separate units.

Initial static mode used pure-runtime freestanding/no-builtin flags,which introduced external CRT memory symbols from Windows SDK macros. Changed frontend object to accepted DLL configuration; strict consumer links now import only GDI32/KERNEL32/USER32. Initial failed capture-build artifacts are archived separately.

GNU objdump export reader handles ordinal/base/hint format; both archives and strict consumer DLLs checked. Previous actual source builds but is rejected for missing private factory ABI; this is an artifact-level negative control,not a runtime mutation count.

Real XP loader unloads/reloads private consumer while ordinary device survives. Exact six unique live wire handles and three explicit device/declaration retirements verified; same session tuple and one final SessionEnd plus driver owner release.
Both GPU runs check zero device/resource maps inside onSessionEnd before its fallback cleanup,and again before genuine owner release. All320 independently expected pixels match.

No production/build/SDK change after accepted115-second XP. D3D8 object wrapping is the next migration step; this stage does not claim D3D8 device/resource delegation or overall stages4/5/6 completion.
